WoW: Forever

Protection Warrior

Shield tanking, and one of Forever's three tanks. Three of its talents now check for a shield, which costs Classic's dual-wield threat build its best threat talents — though Blizzard has deliberately kept a non-shield path to the middle of the tree.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated October 5, 2026 · Beta build 1.60.1.70124 · Null Ossuary

Levelling guide, 1 to 60. The beta is capped at level 30 as of the October 1 build, which Blizzard raised from 20 that day, so no level-60 Protection build has been tested. One live caveat: Blizzard's September 24 notes swapped BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. (row 5) and Focused RageFocused RageTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your offensive abilities by 3. (row 6), so the intended layout is Focused RageFocused RageTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your offensive abilities by 3. in row 5 and BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. in row 6 — the developers' note is "We wanted to give players Focused Rage sooner" — and the client has not applied it yet, so any build touching those rows will move. The September 30 Class Deep Dive lists the pre-swap rows, BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. at 5 and Focused RageFocused RageTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your offensive abilities by 3. at 6, so it records the older layout rather than independently confirming the new one. No source has posted a level 30 build either — the cap only reached 30 on October 1 and none of the three has published one since — so the level 30 line below extends the published level 20 build using the full talent tree's point costs, not a build any guide has recommended. Separately, ClassicWoW.gg flags whether VanguardVanguardTalentCastInstantYour Charge ability is now usable while in Defensive Stance.'s Charge-in-Defensive-Stance works mid-combat as unverified on the live beta; Blizzard's post confirms Charge works in Defensive Stance at all but does not address the mid-combat question either way. Blizzard's own caveat covers all of it: "class abilities and talents may continue to evolve throughout the beta test and are subject to additional changes."

What Protection is for

Shield tanking, and one of Forever's three tanks. The shield is the engine: Shield SpecializationShield SpecializationTalentCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your chance to block attacks with a shield by 1% and increases the amount blocked by 5%. at 5/5 returns 5 Rage on every block, where Classic gave 1, and DefianceDefianceTalentCastInstantIncreases all threat generated in Defensive stance by an additional 15% while a shield is equipped., BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. and Master of DefenseMaster of DefenseTalentCastInstantGenerate 5 Rage when you Dodge or Parry while you have a shield equipped. all now check that you are holding one.

Icy Veins holds both halves at once: "extremely slow when it comes to solo leveling," but "takes less damage and can handle dangerous pulls more safely." This makes solo levelling more forgiving even while it's slower, and its Levelling score (2.5/5) is the highest of the three Warrior specs on Icy Veins' scale — no other source scores them. Fewer kills per minute, far less time sitting down. That dungeons are where the spec pays off is our own reading; no source ranks the three Warrior specs for group play.

Worth knowing before you commit: a full Protection spec is not required to tank at low level.

The Rage rework favours Protection specifically. Blizzard kept the old formula for Rage gained from taking damage but now calculates it as if every Warrior always had 50% damage reduction from Armor — so stacking Armor, which is what this spec does, no longer shrinks your Rage income the way it did in Classic. Damage-absorption effects like Power Word: Shield also stop blocking Rage gain.

The October 1 build also reshuffled this tree, and said why: "Our goal is to give non-shield users a clear path to the middle of the tree, where Protection could serve as a PvP tech secondary specialization, with more access to Improved Bloodrage, Iron Will, Improved Disarm, Last Stand, and Improved Shield Bash." That is a PvP framing more than a levelling one, but it moved rows our build order below assumed — see Your talent points and What Forever changed.

Your talent points

Level 20: 0/0/11. Wowhead and Icy Veins agree on the first ten points and split on the last.

  1. Shield SpecializationShield SpecializationTalentCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your chance to block attacks with a shield by 1% and increases the amount blocked by 5%., 5 points, taken mainly for 5 rage on every block
  2. Improved Thunder ClapImproved Thunder ClapTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your Thunder Clap ability by 6., 3 points for cheaper area threat, now usable in Defensive Stance
  3. Improved BloodrageImproved BloodrageTalentCastInstantIncreases all the Rage generated by your Bloodrage ability by 50%., 2 points — the October 1 build moved this talent to row 1 (it was row 2), so as of this build it no longer needs a single point parked elsewhere first; the published Wowhead/Icy Veins order already takes it this early regardless
  4. The eleventh point is where the two sources part ways. Icy Veins spends it on Master of DefenseMaster of DefenseTalentCastInstantGenerate 5 Rage when you Dodge or Parry while you have a shield equipped., which grants a chance of 5 rage when you Dodge or Parry with a shield equipped — Blizzard publishes no proc chance. Wowhead puts it in Improved RevengeImproved RevengeTalentCastInstantIncreases damage dealt by your Revenge ability by 60%. instead (redesigned to increase Revenge's damage rather than stun, with no figure published; now row 2, moved down from row 3 on October 1 — so this pick got easier to reach, not harder) and explicitly argues against Master of DefenseMaster of DefenseTalentCastInstantGenerate 5 Rage when you Dodge or Parry while you have a shield equipped. at level 20, reasoning that ~10% total avoidance makes its proc too rare to be worth a point yet; Wowhead names Last StandLast StandTalentCastInstantCooldown180 sec cooldownWhen activated, this ability temporarily grants you 30% of your maximum health for 20 sec. After the effect expires, the health is lost. as its own stated alternative for that point.

Level 30: 0/0/21 — our own extension, not a published build, reaching VanguardVanguardTalentCastInstantYour Charge ability is now usable while in Defensive Stance.: Shield SpecializationShield SpecializationTalentCastInstantDurationUntil cancelledIncreases your chance to block attacks with a shield by 1% and increases the amount blocked by 5%. 5, AnticipationAnticipationTalentCastInstantIncreases your Defense Skill by 20. 4, Improved BloodrageImproved BloodrageTalentCastInstantIncreases all the Rage generated by your Bloodrage ability by 50%. 2, Master of DefenseMaster of DefenseTalentCastInstantGenerate 5 Rage when you Dodge or Parry while you have a shield equipped. 2, DefianceDefianceTalentCastInstantIncreases all threat generated in Defensive stance by an additional 15% while a shield is equipped. 3, Improved Sunder ArmorImproved Sunder ArmorTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your Sunder Armor ability by 3. 3, VanguardVanguardTalentCastInstantYour Charge ability is now usable while in Defensive Stance. 1 — twenty points, and the twenty-first is a choice we will not make for you. BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. is out of reach: the September 24 swap puts it in row 6, which is 25 points into the tree. Focused RageFocused RageTalentCastInstantReduces the Rage cost of your offensive abilities by 3. takes its place in row 5 once that swap reaches the client, and until it does, a point in any row you have already opened is the honest answer — no source publishes a level-30 Protection build, and we are not inventing a row for a talent Blizzard has not placed. One ordering note from the October 1 reshuffle: AnticipationAnticipationTalentCastInstantIncreases your Defense Skill by 20. moved from row 1 to row 2 (it now needs points spent elsewhere first) while Improved BloodrageImproved BloodrageTalentCastInstantIncreases all the Rage generated by your Bloodrage ability by 50%. moved the opposite way, row 2 to row 1 — the total points above are unchanged, but if you are levelling this live, bank Improved BloodrageImproved BloodrageTalentCastInstantIncreases all the Rage generated by your Bloodrage ability by 50%. first and AnticipationAnticipationTalentCastInstantIncreases your Defense Skill by 20. once you've unlocked row 2, not the other way around as the old row layout implied.

New in this tree as of October 1: Iron WillIron WillTalentCastInstantReduces the duration of Stun and Fear effects inflicted on you by 15%., landing in row 1. It reduces the duration of Stuns against you rather than resisting them, and it is not in either build above — Blizzard's own framing for the reshuffle (see above) pitches it at a non-shield PvP-secondary path, not the shield-tanking line this page follows. Worth a point if you expect PvP; skip it for pure levelling and dungeon tanking.

Stat priority

Weapon damage, Hit, Strength, Agility, Armor, Stamina, then crit, crit above Agility if you care only about threat (Icy Veins' published order).

Hit now improves TauntTauntLevel 10 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantRangeMeleeCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration3 secTaunts the target to attack you, but has no effect if the target is already attacking you. reliability, which is a Forever-specific reason to value it.

At level 60

Unknown. Whether shield-only tanking holds up now that DefianceDefianceTalentCastInstantIncreases all threat generated in Defensive stance by an additional 15% while a shield is equipped. and BastionBastionTalentCastInstantIncreases all damage you deal by 10% while a shield is equipped. require a shield is untested, and Icy Veins is explicit that its stat priority and gear picks are Level 20 snapshots, not an endgame ranking — Forever reworked dungeon loot and item stats wholesale, so nothing past 20 has been playtested by any of the three sources.

Sources

Compiled from the three major Forever guide sites and cross-checked against each other. Where Blizzard has published an official class deep dive, that post outranks all three and the page is written from it. Everything else — talent ranks, tooltip values, what exists in the tree at all — is settled against the client itself, read through foreverchanges.pro and wago.tools. Where the guides disagree with each other, this page says which said what.
